text:
King's College London was founded in 1829, in response to the theological controversy surrounding the secular London University, as a Tory response intended to reaffirm the established order's educational values. The institution enjoys patronage from the monarch and has had its administrative structure evolve, moving from a proprietorial body to a non-profit one via the King's College London Act 1882.
Over time, King's College London has grown significantly, establishing various academic faculties such as Arts and Humanities, Life Sciences and Medicine, and Dentistry, Oral and Craniofacial Sciences. Key developments include its crucial contributions to the discovery of the double helix structure of DNA in 1953. In 2007, King's gained independent degree-awarding powers from the University of London. The college operates across five campuses in central London and is a member of the Russell Group.
